text: If you hide one hundred thousand dollars under your floor, so the I.R.S. never sees it, you just built tax evasion. But cash never stays hidden. The moment you spend it, it leaves a trail. Buy a car with more than ten thousand in cash, and the dealer has to report it. Deposit it, and the bank has to report it too. Even your neighbor can report you online, without giving a name. Get caught, and you pay it all back, plus a seventy five percent fraud penalty, and up to five years in prison. So let's rewind, and build it legally. Put money in a four oh one K, and up to twenty four thousand five hundred a year skips tax today. An H.S.A. is tax free going in, tax free while it grows, and tax free for medical bills. In a Roth I.R.A., the growth is never taxed. Rent out your home for fourteen days or less a year, and that rent is tax free. Give each kid up to nineteen thousand dollars a year, with no gift tax. And watch the last one, because it has a twist. Live in your home two of the last five years, and up to two hundred fifty thousand dollars of profit is tax free when you sell. Five years. The same number as the prison sentence. Same money. One is a crime. The other is just reading the rules. So where's yours? Under the floor, in a four oh one K, a Roth, or an H.S.A.? Comment one.
